statement: enforcer-plan (b03/b06 precedent) already has TWO byte-identical private copies of a `{{name}}`-placeholder `render()` function (crate::templates::render_template and crate::agents_forest::render) because neither is `pub`. x05 adds a THIRD copy in lessons.rs for the same reason. This is deliberate per-module isolation (no shared-file coupling across b01-b06/x05), not an oversight, but any future refactor that tries to unify these must account for at least three call sites, not one.
why: A future pack (or a well-meaning cleanup pass) may see three near-identical `render()` functions and 'simplify' them into one shared helper, which would violate the workpack's explicit disjoint-ownership model (each feature pack owns its own copy specifically so it has zero shared-file edit surface with siblings). Worth flagging before someone 'fixes' this.
howToApply: When reviewing enforcer-plan for duplication, do not merge templates::render_template / agents_forest::render / lessons::render into one shared function unless a plan owner explicitly re-scopes the disjoint-ownership contract across b03/b06/x05 — the duplication is the isolation mechanism, not debt.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-plan/src/templates.rs render_template (private); crates/enforcer-plan/src/agents_forest.rs render (private, byte-identical contract); crates/enforcer-plan/src/lessons.rs render (this pack, same contract)

statement: Running the real seed-corpus doctor test (`run_doctor` over the actual L1..L26 rows from refs/orchestration-lessons.md) confirmed the honest verdict the workpack asked for: several rows (L9, L10, L15, L20, L25 — all Code-domain, ships-via mentions rule/d-track surfaces) correctly fail closed as Severity::Error because no d01 RuleCandidate fixtures exist yet for them anywhere in the workspace, and rows whose ships-via text matches none of the sniffer's keywords (e.g. L1's 'fixed MCP tool behavior (arc-16)') correctly land as PlanDoc-only and warn rather than being force-mapped into a route the row never actually declared. This is the intended non-fabricated result, not a bug to silence.
why: A future worker or reviewer running `cargo test -p enforcer-plan lessons::real_seed_corpus_imports_and_doctor_reports_honest_verdict` might see non-empty error/warning findings and assume the doctor or importer is broken. It is working exactly as specified: the seed corpus's own Code-domain/RuleCandidate rows have no fixtures yet (that is a real, pending gap for whichever future pack builds d01 rule candidates from these lessons), and ships-via prose that matches no keyword honestly falls back to PlanDoc rather than guessing.
howToApply: Do not 'fix' the real-corpus test by loosening the sniffer's keyword matching or by pre-registering fake fixtures just to make it green — the workpack explicitly asked for an honest verdict, including legitimately-pending rows. If a future pack lands real fixtures for L9/L10/L15/L20/L25, THAT is when this test's error count should drop, and the test will reflect it automatically (it computes findings live, not a pinned count).

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-plan lessons::real_seed_corpus_imports_and_doctor_reports_honest_verdict -- passed with non-empty errors+warnings by design

statement: The legacy coordination CLI fallback (scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination claim/message) echoes context.hub back as the literal string '--lane' (an arg-parsing artifact) instead of the passed --hub value, in both the claim and message JSON responses observed during this lane's run. The claim/message themselves succeeded with the correct lane/paths/branch, so this looks cosmetic, but it means context.hub is NOT reliable for any caller trying to verify which hub an event landed in from the response alone.
why: L2 in the seed corpus already flags 'hub context must record CALLER identity, not server-side resolution' as a fixed finding for arc-16 — this is a second, still-open instance of context metadata not reflecting the caller's actual input, in the CLI-fallback path rather than the MCP path L2 addressed. Worth a follow-up ticket against the legacy .mjs coordination CLI arg parser.
howToApply: When using the ocentra_enforcer_run/CLI-fallback path for coordination claim or message (as required whenever the MCP server reports stale), do not trust response.event.context.hub for verification — cross-check against the --hub value you actually passed, or inspect .ledger/<hub>/ on disk directly.

evidence.ref: node scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination claim --hub enforcer-rust-build ... returned event.context.hub == "--lane" and event.hub == "--lane" in both claim and message calls this session
